name: Generate a runnable desktop data product from intent

checks.check: Read inferred_model.json and the supplied CSV headers before authoring.
Create spec.py, models.py, infra-profile.yaml, transform/main.py, requirements.txt, and a relative csv-source-path. Do not author deployment-spec.yaml, manifest.yaml, or models.yaml.
Do not alter supplied CSV headers or rows to manufacture a primary key.

Every promised physical BASE model declares one or more existing source columns with primary_key(); semantic views are exempt. Accept a validated composite key, but never synthesize a key for a base model.

A DERIVED model (promised, computed in the transform, no data/<name>/ directory) declares the key its derivation's grain implies, constructed deterministically from source values plus the grain's ordinal — never a UUID. A dedupe keeps its source key; only a regrain declares a new composite. The key must be unique and non-null over the landed rows.

Derived rows reach DuckDB as @dlt.resource generators named from duckdb.model_tables, appended to the SAME resources list and landed by ONE pipeline.run(..., write_disposition='replace'). The DDL ban is not relaxed: no duckdb.connect write, no CREATE TABLE/VIEW, no direct file write into staging.

Derived resources yield plain FLAT dicts of scalars — never a pandas/polars DataFrame (the pinned venv has no pyarrow) and never a nested dict or list (dlt would emit a parent__field child table). Imports stay within pandas, duckdb, and the stdlib; output is deterministic across reruns.

Each derived model carries an in-transform assert over the source-vs-derived relationship, raised with actual-vs-expected before the rows are yielded — restating the transform's own arithmetic does not count. It is the in-transform data-quality gate and is mandatory even when the closure also declares executable contracts; never loosen one to make a run pass.
Use public semantic_model/semantic_view/metric_field APIs. Base models own keys, dimensions, and joins; views own metrics. No private nxd.spec imports or __nxd_semantic__ metadata writes.

Every description supplied by inferred_model.json survives into models.py: each model with a description declares one via semantic_model(...).description(...) (preferred) or the description= constructor kwarg, and each dimension/metric role placed with a description carries a non-empty description. Placing a role with its name but not its description is a fail — describe_model is the only surface the querying agent reads, so the concept arrives as a bare label.

Descriptions are written INSIDE the role builder — dimension(description=...) / metric(description=...). A description= on the enclosing field(...) or metric_field(...) is an attribute description that never reaches describe_model, so it is a fail even though the text is present in the file.
Promise every physical model — base and derived alike — register views with .model(...), use output port duckdb and no .semantic_tools() call.

PHYSICAL_MODELS is the set of landed tables (BASE_MODELS + DERIVED_MODELS), not the data/ listing: every base model has a data/<name>/ directory, no derived model does, every data/ directory has a base model, and every PHYSICAL_MODELS entry is promised and resolves through duckdb.model_tables. Build model_tables from PHYSICAL_MODELS, never from the directory listing.

Use dlt through DuckDbOutput, source only from secrets[csv_source], a read-back naming assertion over promised physical models only, run-local dlt state, replace writes, and .transform-complete. Do not ingest or expect semantic views from duckdb.model_tables.
Run check_generated_closure.py against the final closure and obtain ALL CHECKS PASSED.
Do not claim a supervisor build or governed semantic query when the evaluator only executed the transform.
